A calmer look, a progress bar for a build's index, and a fix for putting a whole build into a
library.

**Upgrading:** replace `usnfetch.exe` and start it as usual. Nothing else to do.

## A calmer look

- Fewer coloured pills. States are plain text, and only problems get colour: Found and Verified
  are grey.
- Catalog rows are one line each, with one State column (a download, what's on disk, or the
  health). Open link and Import list are one **Add** menu.
- A build's page: the folder path has its own line, the kind menu sits in front of the search box,
  Sort and Hide what I have are under **View**, and the build's size and systems show at its top.
- Search: one plain Download button per game, with the other way in its arrow. "open it there"
  opens the build at that game.
- The download window keeps the folder name, archives and files already there under **Options**,
  which says how they're set.
- Rarely used things are behind Show advanced now: the status bar's file name, Run setup again,
  Import from SABnzbd once you have a provider, and the Libraries Reloads column. Pause all and the
  speed limit banner are gone from Activity, since the status bar has both.

## See a build's index download

The first time you open a build, it downloads its index, a few GB for a big one. That now shows
like a download, with how much, how fast and how long, in the opening window, the status bar and
Activity. Its speed counts in the total. "Saving its index" shows while the last part is written.

## Fixes

- **Putting a whole build into a library no longer hangs.** It also happened when you just opened
  the download window for a whole build with a library picked, and the build stayed stuck until a
  restart.
- **Reopening a build is quick again.** A saved index that Windows had compressed was unpacked
  every time it opened: 17 seconds for a 20 TB build, now about 1.
- **A build's search starts on Games**, the same search as the Search page, and remembers what you
  pick.
- **Share manifests are checked the way the official app checks them.** A link that names the
  share's owner only opens a signed manifest, or an old v3 one, so one that was changed on its way
  to you is refused instead of being read as unsigned.
- Smaller ones: the status bar's link goes straight to the build, paused shows Paused, Enter
  queues a download again, Search's menu stays on screen on phones, and a build's buttons move to
  their own line instead of being cut off.
